m1.alt: The Crab Nebula: a tangled orange and blue cloud of filaments around a bright core, in a Hubble mosaic.
m1.author: NASA, ESA, J. Hester and A. Loll (Arizona State University)
m1.note: A Hubble composite: neutral oxygen mapped to blue, sulfur to green, doubly ionized oxygen to red, not colours the eye would see.

m8.alt: The Lagoon Nebula: a wide pink and red cloud of glowing gas crossed by dark lanes, from the VLT Survey Telescope.
m8.author: ESO/VPHAS+ team

m13.alt: The Hercules globular cluster: a dense round swarm of hundreds of thousands of stars, brightest at the centre.
m13.author: Chuck Ayoub

m31.alt: The Andromeda Galaxy: a tilted spiral with a yellow core, blue outer arms and dark dust lanes, with two small companion galaxies.
m31.author: Brody Wesner

m42.alt: The Orion Nebula: a bright teal and red cloud of gas around the Trapezium stars, in a Hubble mosaic.
m42.author: NASA, ESA, M. Robberto (Space Telescope Science Institute/ESA) and the Hubble Space Telescope Orion Treasury Project Team
m42.note: A composite of visible and near-infrared filters plus an H-alpha filter, not a single visible-light exposure.

m44.alt: The Beehive Cluster: a loose scatter of bright white and yellow stars against a dark field.
m44.author: Chuck Ayoub

m45.alt: The Pleiades: seven bright blue stars wrapped in wispy blue reflection nebulosity.
m45.author: NASA, ESA, AURA/Caltech, Palomar Observatory

m51.alt: The Whirlpool Galaxy: a face-on spiral with pink star-forming knots along its arms, joined to a small yellow companion galaxy, from Hubble.
m51.author: NASA and European Space Agency

m57.alt: The Ring Nebula seen by Webb's NIRCam: a glowing ring of gas with a faint star at its centre.
m57.author: ESA/Webb, NASA, CSA, M. Barlow, N. Cox, R. Wesson
m57.sourceTitle: Webb captures detailed beauty of Ring Nebula (NIRCam image) (weic2320b).jpg
m57.note: Webb's near-infrared view, not a visible-light photograph.

m87.alt: M87: a smooth, round elliptical galaxy with a straight jet of plasma pointing out from its core, from Hubble.
m87.author: NASA, STScI, WikiSky
m87.note: A composite of visible and infrared observations made to resolve the jet, not a single visible-light photograph.

sgr-a-star.alt: Sagittarius A*: the Event Horizon Telescope's orange ring of light around the dark shadow of the black hole.
sgr-a-star.author: EHT Collaboration
sgr-a-star.note: A radio image from the Event Horizon Telescope, not a photograph in visible light.

hubble-deep-field.alt: The Hubble Deep Field: hundreds of faint galaxies of every shape and colour scattered across a tiny patch of dark sky.
hubble-deep-field.author: Robert Williams (NASA, ESA, STScI)

m16.alt: The Eagle Nebula: dark pillars of dust rising into a red glowing cloud, from ESO's La Silla observatory.
m16.author: ESO

m20.alt: The Trifid Nebula: a pink emission cloud split by three dark lanes, beside a blue reflection nebula, from the Rubin Observatory.
m20.author: RubinObs/NOIRLab/SLAC/NSF/DOE/AURA

m27.alt: The Dumbbell Nebula: a round green shell of gas with pink edges, crossed by a scatter of foreground stars, from NOIRLab.
m27.author: REU program/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA

m33.alt: The Triangulum Galaxy: a loose face-on spiral with a bright white core and red star-forming regions, from the VLT Survey Telescope.
m33.author: ESO
m33.sourceTitle: VST snaps a very detailed view of the Triangulum Galaxy.jpg
m33.note: A composite that adds a narrowband H-alpha filter to broadband colour, so its red gas clouds read brighter than true colour.

m78.alt: M78: two bright blue reflection nebulae lit by young stars, with dark dust clouds around them, from ESO.
m78.author: ESO/Igor Chekalin
m78.note: A composite that adds a narrowband hydrogen filter to broadband colour, so its red gas glows brighter than true colour.

m81.alt: Bode's Galaxy: a grand-design spiral with a yellow core and blue arms, from Hubble.
m81.author: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

m82.alt: The Cigar Galaxy: an edge-on disk with red filaments of gas blown out above and below it, from Hubble.
m82.author: NASA, ESA, and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)
m82.note: A composite of visible, infrared and hydrogen-emission filters, not a single visible-light exposure.

m104.alt: The Sombrero Galaxy: a bright bulge with a dark dust ring seen almost edge-on, from Hubble.
m104.author: ESA/Hubble & NASA, K. Noll

horsehead.alt: The Horsehead Nebula: a dark horse-head-shaped cloud silhouetted against a red glowing background, from ESO's SPECULOOS telescopes.
horsehead.author: ESO
horsehead.sourceTitle: Nebulosa testa di cavallo con SPECULOOS.jpg

flame.alt: The Flame Nebula: an orange glowing cloud cut by a dark lane of dust, beside a bright star.
flame.author: Chuck Ayoub

ngc869.alt: The Double Cluster: two dense groups of bright blue-white stars side by side.
ngc869.author: Markus Pössel

ngc884.alt: The Double Cluster: two neighbouring clusters of blue-white stars in one wide field.
ngc884.author: Genuson

ngc7000.alt: The North America Nebula: a red emission cloud shaped like the continent, with the Pelican Nebula beside it.
ngc7000.author: gjdonatiello

ngc6960.alt: The western Veil Nebula: thin red and blue filaments of a supernova remnant, from the WIYN 0.9-metre telescope.
ngc6960.author: T. A. Rector/University of Alaska Anchorage and WIYN/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA
ngc6960.note: A narrowband composite: hydrogen mapped to red, oxygen to blue, sulfur to green, not colours the eye would see.

ngc6992.alt: The eastern Veil Nebula: bright braided filaments of red and blue-green gas, from the WIYN 0.9-metre telescope.
ngc6992.author: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and WIYN/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA
ngc6992.note: A narrowband composite: oxygen mapped to blue, sulfur to green, hydrogen to orange, not colours the eye would see.

milky-way.alt: The Milky Way's band arching over ESO's Very Large Telescope, with a laser guide star pointed at the galactic centre.
milky-way.author: ESO/Y. Beletsky

mercury.alt: Mercury: a grey, heavily cratered planet in true colour from MESSENGER.
mercury.author: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Arizona State University/Carnegie Institution of Washington
mercury.note: A composite of three narrow-band filters assigned to blue, green and red, MESSENGER's own approximation of true colour.

venus.alt: Venus: a pale yellow-white globe of unbroken cloud, from Mariner 10.
venus.author: NASA/JPL-Caltech

mars.alt: Mars: a rust-red planet with a white polar cap and dark surface markings.
mars.author: Kevin Gill from Los Angeles, CA, United States
mars.sourceTitle: Mars - August 30 2021 - Flickr - Kevin M. Gill.png

jupiter.alt: Jupiter: banded cream and brown clouds with the Great Red Spot, from Hubble's 2024 OPAL programme.
jupiter.author: NASA/STSCI (S.T.A.R.S)

saturn.alt: Saturn: the pale gold planet with its rings wide open, from Cassini.
saturn.author: NASA / JPL-Caltech / SSI / color composite by Gordan Ugarkovic (processed by User:Anonymsiy, cropped by User:Nrco0e)
saturn.sourceTitle: Saturn global view from Cassini, rings open Better Colour square crop.png

moon.alt: The full Moon: grey maria and bright highlands with rays from Tycho crater.
moon.author: Gregory H. Revera
moon.note: Shown full; the chart draws the phase for your moment.
